name: Bayesian Inference: Priorfield
subtitle: Bayes nets, HMMs, EM, MCMC
shortDescription: Move the sliders, watch the belief change, then answer questions computed from what you built.
longDescription:
An undergraduate course in probabilistic models and Bayesian inference for your phone. Eight units, about 36 hours, in sessions of 3 to 8 minutes.

You start every unit with a puzzle, then explore a real situation you can manipulate, and only then see the equation that describes what you just watched. Tap any symbol to find it in the picture.

WHAT YOU BUILD AND SEE
- Bayes' rule: a clinic crowd of 1000 dots and a coin-evidence update
- Bayesian networks: a house-alarm network with evidence, explaining away and d-separation
- Naive Bayes: a spam sorter with Laplace smoothing
- Hidden Markov models: guessing the weather from umbrellas, forward and Viterbi
- Latent variables: EM sorting a mixed crowd of shoppers into groups
- Sampling: a night hiker (Metropolis) and darts that estimate pi
- Bayesian estimation: a free-throw shooter and a line with an honest uncertainty band
- Calibration: reliability diagrams, ECE, Brier score and cost-based thresholds

HOW IT TEACHES
- Quizzes are computed from the state of your lab, with a worked reason after every answer
- Wrong answers come back gently in a replay queue; sessions end with a good place to stop
- A belief bar shows your mastery as a probability that updates like the course teaches
- Every claim lists sources with exact sections or lectures (Bishop PRML, Murphy PML, Berkeley CS 188 and DATA C102, CMU 10-708 and 15-281, Stanford CS228 notes, and primary papers); tap one to read it in a window over the lesson
- Text size A- and A+, labels for screen readers, works offline, no account

Free with ads at natural breaks. One optional monthly subscription removes ads and the daily practice limit (7-day free trial). Cancel any time in your App Store or Google Play account settings; cancellation takes effect at the next billing cycle. You can also watch short videos to earn credits.

Written and source-checked by our team; not reviewed by an external expert. Teaching examples (health, triage, spam) are puzzles, not advice. Content as of 2026-11-17.
